f.title: No requirement to scan the Canada Vigilance Online Database or Health Product InfoWatch for ICSRs
f.statement: For individual case safety report (ICSR) reporting obligations under section C.01.017 of the Food and Drug Regulations and section 24 of the Natural Health Products Regulations, MAHs are not required to scan the Canada Vigilance Online Database or the Health Product InfoWatch.
f.clause: Revised guidance > 4.3 Regulatory Authority Sources > Reports from the CV Online Database and the Health Product InfoWatch
f.legal_basis: Food and Drug Regulations C.01.017; Natural Health Products Regulations s. 24
f.applicability: Effective as of the date of posting of the notice (19 February 2026); replaces section 4.3 of the 2018 guidance and the 2020 Notice to Industry
f.systems: Canada Vigilance Online Database; Health Product InfoWatch

rows.actor: Market authorization holder (MAH) for drugs and natural health products
rows.quote: For Individual Case Safety Report (ICSR) reporting obligations (section C.01.017 of the Food and Drug Regulations, and section 24 of the Natural Health Products Regulations), MAHs are not required to scan the CV Online Database or the Health Product InfoWatch.

No other change. Double-check: confirmed statement, actor and legal basis against the quote. Below 90: 'not required to' is an exemption, so Permitted is a judgement call; the applicability (effective date, replacement of the old section 4.3 and the 2020 notice) comes from the Objective and Implementation sections, not the quote.

f.title: Report foreign serious unexpected adverse reaction reports, including those from foreign regulators
f.statement: You must report to Health Canada individual serious unexpected adverse reaction reports that occurred outside Canada, for example those originating from foreign regulatory authorities.
f.clause: Revised guidance > 4.3 Regulatory Authority Sources > Reports from foreign regulatory authority databases
f.applicability: Serious unexpected adverse reactions occurring outside Canada, including reports from foreign regulatory authority databases
f.exceptions: Not required where you can determine from the Exclusion Criteria for Product Identification that the product is not yours (HC-NOTICE43-2026-0003); if you cannot determine it, presume it is yours and report (HC-NOTICE43-2026-0004).

rows.actor: Market authorization holder (MAH) for drugs and natural health products
rows.quote: You must report to Health Canada individual serious unexpected adverse reaction reports, which occurred outside of Canada; for example, those originating from foreign regulatory authorities.
rows.location: Revised guidance > 4.3 Regulatory Authority Sources > Reports from foreign regulatory authority databases
rows.review_note: Review: added the exclusion-criteria exemption (HC-NOTICE43-2026-0003) and the presumption fallback (HC-NOTICE43-2026-0004) as exceptions, so the duty reads with its conditions. Level Mandatory ('must') kept. Double-check: confirmed; 'you must report' and the notice's definition of 'you' as MAHs support Mandatory and the actor. No deadline is stated in the notice, so deadline stays empty.

f.title: ICSRs from foreign databases need not be submitted when exclusion criteria show the product is not yours
f.statement: You are not required to submit ICSRs from foreign regulatory authority databases if you can determine that the product is not yours based on the Exclusion Criteria for Product Identification: country of marketing, product name, active ingredient name, pharmaceutical form, batch number, marketing status, or other characteristics.
f.clause: Revised guidance > 4.3 Regulatory Authority Sources > Reports from foreign regulatory authority databases
f.applicability: ICSRs from foreign regulatory authority databases

rows.actor: Market authorization holder (MAH) for drugs and natural health products
rows.quote: You are not required to submit ICSRs from these foreign databases if you can determine that the product is not yours, based on the following “Exclusion Criteria for Product Identification”: country of marketing, product name, active ingredient name, pharmaceutical form, batch number, marketing status, or other characteristics.
rows.location: Revised guidance > 4.3 Regulatory Authority Sources > Reports from foreign regulatory authority databases
rows.review_note: Review: 'not required to submit' kept as Permitted (express exemption to the duty in HC-NOTICE43-2026-0002, with its own decision criteria). Kept as a separate row because it carries the criteria list; cross-referenced from 0002's exceptions. Double-check: confirmed; the criteria list matches the quote. Below 90: 'not required to submit' is an exemption, so Permitted is a judgement call.

f.title: Presume the product is yours when it cannot be identified and say the brand was not identified
f.statement: If you are unable to determine whether the product is yours, you should presume that it is, report the ICSR to Health Canada, and indicate that you could not identify the specific brand.
f.clause: Revised guidance > 4.3 Regulatory Authority Sources > Reports from foreign regulatory authority databases
f.applicability: Foreign ICSRs where product ownership cannot be determined

f.title: Exclusion criteria may be applied to foreign reports from any source and override sections 2.1.2 and 4.1.3
f.statement: You may also apply the Exclusion Criteria for Product Identification to foreign adverse reaction reports from any source, for example scientific literature reports. These exclusion criteria override the criteria in sections 2.1.2 (Foreign Adverse Reaction Reports) and 4.1.3 (Scientific Literature Reports) of the Reporting Adverse Reactions to Marketed Health Products - Guidance Document for Industry (2018).
f.clause: Revised guidance > 4.3 Regulatory Authority Sources > Note
f.applicability: Foreign adverse reaction reports from any source, including scientific literature
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; Safety intake & collection
